transactions.title: Explorer
transactions.unstake_claim_nft_tooltip: This NFT is your withdrawal receipt (Stake Claim). The network generates it automatically as proof, and you must keep it in your wallet to claim your XRD once the waiting period ends.
transactions.claim_nft_presented_tooltip: NFT automatically generated by the network and sent to the user to be used as proof to claim their XRD once the waiting period ends.
transactions.claim_nft_redeemed_tooltip: This NFT has been successfully redeemed and permanently destroyed by the network. In exchange, the corresponding XRD tokens have been deposited into your account.
transactions.claim_nft_authorized_tooltip: You have presented this Stake Claim NFT to the validator's smart contract as proof of ownership to authorize the release of your XRD tokens.
transactions.proposer_tooltip: In each turn, the Proposer collects transactions and assembles a draft block. The rest of the validators audit and sign it (vote). Only when the block gathers signatures from more than 2/3 of the network, it is definitively approved (Committed). Due to this teamwork, rewards are shared between the proposer and the validators.

well_known_tooltips.xrd: Radix native token (XRD). It is the main resource of the network; used to pay transaction fees (gas) and to secure the network through validator staking.
well_known_tooltips.secp256k1_signature_virtual_badge: secp256k1 signature virtual badge. Dynamically generated by the engine to cryptographically prove that a transaction was signed with an external key (e.g., Ethereum style). Used to validate access.
well_known_tooltips.ed25519_signature_virtual_badge: Ed25519 signature virtual badge. Proves to the system that the user successfully signed using Ed25519 cryptography (Radix's native standard). Used to authenticate calls and authorize spending.
well_known_tooltips.system_transaction_badge: System transaction badge. Grants superuser privileges. Used internally by Radix to execute high-level protocol operations (such as epoch changes or token emission).
well_known_tooltips.package_of_direct_caller_virtual_badge: Direct caller package badge. Proves which contract made the immediate call in the code. Useful for restricting private functions exclusively to components belonging to the same original package.
well_known_tooltips.global_caller_virtual_badge: Global caller badge. Certifies that the execution call comes directly from the global transaction space. Used to manage cross-context validations within the Radix Engine.
well_known_tooltips.package_owner_badge: Package owner badge. Represents absolute ownership rights over a deployed code (Package). Used to authorize future code updates or modify its metadata.
well_known_tooltips.validator_owner_badge: Validator owner badge. Accredits control over a validator node on the network. Whoever holds it can change its fees, reconfigure it, or unregister it from the consensus system.
well_known_tooltips.account_owner_badge: Account owner badge. Accredits control over a user's bank account/wallet. Essential for authorizing fund withdrawals and changes to account permissions.
well_known_tooltips.identity_owner_badge: Identity owner badge. Proves authority over a Persona (Web3 Identity). Used in dApps for passwordless authentication (Radix Connect) and user data management.
well_known_tooltips.package_package: Package management package. Contains the core logic on how smart contracts (Blueprints) are compiled, published, updated, and interconnected on the Radix network.
well_known_tooltips.resource_package: Resource package. The engine behind all assets on Radix. Defines how tokens, NFTs, and badges are created, minted, burned, and transferred.
well_known_tooltips.account_package: Account package. Contains the standard Blueprint that defines how user wallets/accounts work, controlling rules for deposits, withdrawals, and asset locking.
well_known_tooltips.identity_package: Identity package. Defines the Blueprints for 'Personas' on Radix. Facilitates session and dApp access management by separating digital identity from financial funds.
well_known_tooltips.consensus_manager_package: Consensus manager package. Code that governs the rules for validator nodes, staking registration, delegation, and network emission reward distribution.
well_known_tooltips.access_controller_package: Access controller package. Manages advanced security policies, allowing the configuration of multi-signatures (multisig) and social recovery processes for accounts and identities.
well_known_tooltips.transaction_processor_package: Transaction processor package. Contains the logic that measures computational cost, charges network fees, and applies execution limits in the Radix Engine.
well_known_tooltips.metadata_module_package: Metadata module package. Defines a standardized system to store, read, and update descriptive information (names, symbols, URLs) on any component or token in the network.
well_known_tooltips.royalty_module_package: Royalty module package. Code that allows dApp developers to automatically collect fees whenever their smart contracts are interacted with.
well_known_tooltips.role_assignment_module_package: Role assignment module package. Centralizes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) logic. Decides which badges have permission to execute specific functions within a component.
well_known_tooltips.genesis_helper_package: Genesis helper package. Native logic used exclusively in the network's initial block (Genesis) to pre-configure the global state and distribute initial funds.
well_known_tooltips.faucet_package: Faucet package. Contains the source code for a public token dispenser. Primarily useful on test networks (Testnets) for requesting free funds.
well_known_tooltips.pool_package: Pool package. Implements the standards to create decentralized liquidity pools (1, 2, or multi-token). It is the foundation of the DeFi system and DEXs on Radix.
well_known_tooltips.transaction_tracker_package: Transaction tracker package. Code that allows contracts to inspect metadata of executed transactions, useful for tracking histories and preventing manipulation.
well_known_tooltips.locker_package: Account locker package. Creates secure storage spaces for airdrops or delayed withdrawals, where a user can claim their tokens on-demand and securely.
well_known_tooltips.test_utils_package: Test utilities package. A set of integrated functions and tools to facilitate simulations, debugging, and dApp testing by developers.
well_known_tooltips.consensus_manager: Consensus manager component. The 'live' global instance that actively executes staking, coordinates current validators, and processes XRD emission (rewards) every epoch.
well_known_tooltips.genesis_helper: Genesis helper component. Single-use entity that ran when the Radix Mainnet launched to inject the initial state and migrate previous balances to the public network.
well_known_tooltips.faucet: Faucet component. The entity that dispenses tokens. Although the address exists on Mainnet, its usage is disabled on live networks to prevent the creation of fake money.
well_known_tooltips.transaction_tracker: Transaction tracker component. Live global entity used internally by the Radix node to maintain record integrity, preventing double-spending or replay attacks.

type_tooltips.account: Account Address. Acts as a user wallet that holds tokens, NFTs, and other resources. It is protected by access rules and cryptographic signatures.
type_tooltips.resource: Resource Address. Represents the definition of an asset on the network. It can be a fungible token (cryptocurrency), an NFT (unique asset), or a permission badge.
type_tooltips.component: Component Address. An active ('live') smart contract on the network. It contains dApp logic and has its own local state to store data or funds inside it.
type_tooltips.package: Package Address. Contains the source code (Blueprints) uploaded by a developer. It does not hold funds or user data; it serves as a template to instantiate Components.
type_tooltips.validator: Validator Address. A network node in charge of processing transactions and securing consensus. Users can stake their XRD on this validator.
type_tooltips.identity: Identity Address (Persona). Represents a user's digital profile in Web3, used for secure passwordless login to dApps.

transactions.nft_withdrawn_title: This NFT ({id}) was withdrawn/sent in this transaction
transactions.consensus_manager_info_body: The Consensus Manager is a native built-in component of the Radix protocol. It does not belong to any user — it is the system engine that manages epochs, block proposal cycles, and staking reward distribution. When it appears as Origin, it means the protocol itself is distributing XRD (e.g. network emissions to validators or delegators). It does not have a standard user address; its address is a special system constant.
transactions.method_minted_title: These assets were generated or minted out of thin air during this transaction, with no prior sender.
transactions.method_network_title: These assets were transferred by a network-level component (e.g., Consensus Manager) as a result of a network action, such as staking rewards.
transactions.method_smart_contract_title: These assets were directly sent by a Smart Contract (Component), such as a liquidity pool or a dApp.
transactions.method_staking_title: These assets were released by a validator's staking component as a result of a claim, unstake, or staking operation.
transactions.method_user_title: These assets were withdrawn from one or more user accounts to be sent to this address.
transactions.net_summary_desc: Displays aggregated inputs and outputs for your account (if applicable).
transactions.fees_distribution_desc: Breakdown of how transaction fees were distributed by the protocol.
transactions.tx_flow_info_title: How to read our transaction flow
transactions.tx_flow_info_desc_1: In the Web3 ecosystem, transactions are rarely one-way transfers. Usually, they are swaps (you give something to receive something else).
transactions.tx_flow_info_desc_2: That is why, in our interface, the columns do not separate "what goes out" from "what comes in", but rather group the movements according to the Role of the Actors:
transactions.tx_flow_info_left_col_desc: This column represents the entity that initiates the action. Here we group all net changes that this account undergoes in the transaction, both positive and negative.
transactions.tx_flow_info_left_col_example: Example: If you initiate a swap, in this same column you will see that -10 XRD goes out and at the same time +1 NFT comes in. Both data are here because they belong to the final balance of the account that originated the action.
transactions.tx_flow_info_right_col_title: RIGHT COLUMN: Destination Address (The Receiver / Counterparty)
transactions.tx_flow_info_right_col_desc: This column represents the entity or smart contract to which the main action is directed. Like the origin, it shows the total impact on that account.
transactions.tx_flow_info_right_col_example: Example: If the account receiving the transaction is the one that assumes the payment of commissions (fees), you will see that negative value reflected here, in the destination column.

transactions.fees_proposer_title: XRD awarded to the validator that proposed this block. Receives 25% of Execution, Storage, and Finalization + 100% of Tips.
transactions.fees_validator_title: XRD distributed proportionally among the active validator set. 25% of Execution, Storage, and Finalization costs.

transactions.lock_fee_desc: You authorized the network to spend up to {max} XRD. The actual fee charged was {actual} XRD, so the rest was automatically returned.
transactions.lock_fee_title: In Radix, fees are not charged arbitrarily. The user must pre-authorize a maximum fee (lock_fee). If execution costs less, the remaining XRD is automatically returned. If it would cost more, the transaction fails without overcharging.
transactions.fee_execution_title: Computational cost of processing the transaction logic, smart contract calls, and oracle queries.
transactions.fee_storage_title: Cost of storing data on the ledger nodes. Calculated using the internal XRD/USD oracle price.
transactions.fee_finalization_title: Cost of signature verification and transaction finalization.
transactions.fee_royalty_cost_title: 100% paid to the Blueprint/Component developer as usage fees.
transactions.fee_tips_cost_title: Optional tip from the sender. 100% goes to the block proposer validator.
transactions.auth_badge_desc: In Radix, security is resource-oriented. To execute protected methods (like updating oracle prices), the caller must show a physical proof (badge) of authorization. This transaction presents an amount of {amount} of the badge:
transactions.oracle_update_desc: This transaction updates the market prices for multiple assets on an Oracle smart contract.
transactions.oracle_desc: Internal oracle price used by the protocol to calculate storage costs.
transactions.airdrop_desc: This transaction distributes rewards or airdrops to a specific user through a restricted smart contract method.
transactions.summary_resources_desc: Resources, components, and packages involved in this transaction.
transactions.created_entities_desc: New global entities created during this transaction.
transactions.affected_entities_desc: Global entities that were accessed or modified during this transaction.

transactions.protocol_vote_no_badge: No badge proof found in manifest
transactions.protocol_vote_desc: The validator owner presented their owner badge to authorise this protocol update vote on behalf of the validator node.
transactions.behavior_explanation: Derived from the resource's role assignments — what authorities can do with this asset.
transactions.role_tooltip_name: The name of this role and what it controls.
transactions.role_tooltip_type_owner: Requires the owner badge to be presented. Only the owner of this resource can exercise this role.
transactions.role_tooltip_type_allow_all: Anyone can exercise this role — no special authority is needed.
transactions.role_tooltip_type_deny_all: Nobody can exercise this role — this action is permanently disabled.
transactions.role_tooltip_type_explicit: A custom access rule controls who can exercise this role.
transactions.role_tooltip_status_updatable: The assignment of this role can be changed in the future by an authority.
transactions.role_tooltip_status_immutable: The assignment of this role is permanently fixed and cannot be changed.
transactions.role_desc_minter: Can create new tokens and increase supply.
transactions.role_desc_minter_updater: Can update who has the minter role.
transactions.role_desc_burner: Can destroy tokens and reduce supply.
transactions.role_desc_burner_updater: Can update who has the burner role.
transactions.role_desc_freezer: Can freeze/unfreeze token movements in vaults.
transactions.role_desc_freezer_updater: Can update who has the freezer role.
transactions.role_desc_recaller: Can forcibly retrieve tokens from any vault.
transactions.role_desc_recaller_updater: Can update who has the recaller role.
transactions.role_desc_depositor: Controls who can deposit tokens into accounts.
transactions.role_desc_depositor_updater: Can update who has the depositor role.
transactions.role_desc_withdrawer: Controls who can withdraw tokens from accounts.
transactions.role_desc_withdrawer_updater: Can update who has the withdrawer role.
transactions.role_desc_metadata_setter: Can update name, symbol and other metadata.
transactions.role_desc_metadata_setter_updater: Can update who has the metadata setter role.
transactions.role_desc_metadata_locker: Can lock metadata fields to prevent future changes.
transactions.role_desc_metadata_locker_updater: Can update who has the metadata locker role.
transactions.role_desc_owner: Master authority that can exercise all owner-assigned roles.
transactions.behavior_supply_increase: The supply of this asset can be increased.
transactions.behavior_supply_decrease: The supply of this asset can be decreased.
transactions.behavior_supply_fixed: The supply of this asset is fixed.
transactions.behavior_metadata_changeable: Naming and information of this asset can be changed.
transactions.behavior_metadata_fixed: Naming and information of this asset is fixed.
transactions.behavior_withdrawable_restricted: Withdrawals from accounts require special authority.
transactions.behavior_depositable_restricted: Deposits into accounts require special authority.
transactions.behavior_freezable: This asset can be frozen by an authority.
transactions.behavior_recallable: This asset can be recalled from vaults by an authority.
transactions.behavior_nft_data_changeable: NFT data fields can be updated.
